advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Avoid recording receipt resolution predicates for arbitrary historical commit-message refs — resolve referencing-commit candidates through a non-receipting resolver (or restrict recorded resolutions to the accepted close scope).
evidence: close_precheck.py: `resolver_kwargs = {} if ticket_view is None else {"resolver": ticket_view.resolve}` then `commit_impact.referencing_commits(accepted_ids, tracker, str(repo_root), metrics=metrics, **resolver_kwargs)`

commit_impact.py:227-235: `for ref in extract_ticket_refs(message): ... resolved_cache[ref] = (resolver(ref) if resolver is not None else ...)` — resolver is invoked for every ref in every commit in `git log`
ticket_view.py:120-125: `def resolve(...): ... self._receipt_resolution[ref] = {"kind": kind, "value": resolved}` — every resolve call is recorded into the receipt
ticket_receipt.py:169-172 and 398-401: validation replays all `resolutions` and `negative` entries, so any recorded ref that changes resolution becomes a conflict
advisory.finding: Passing `ticket_view.resolve` as the resolver to `referencing_commits` records a resolution predicate (positive AND negative) into the read receipt for EVERY distinct ticket reference found in EVERY commit message across the entire repo history, not just the accepted close scope. `ticket_view.resolve()` unconditionally writes into `self._receipt_resolution` (and negatives are surfaced in the receipt), and `validate_receipt` replays all of them before publication. An unrelated ticket that any historical commit mentions — newly created, renamed, or made resolvable between verify and publish — flips a recorded negative/positive resolution and raises a spurious exit-10 concurrency conflict that forces a fresh (billable) completion run.
scenarios: A completion close on a repo with long history where old commits reference tickets unrelated to the closing ticket; a concurrent create/rename of one of those unrelated tickets between verify and publish
Any close where a historical commit's `rebar-ticket:` trailer names an id that later becomes resolvable
advisory.suggested_fix: Use a resolver that does not mutate the receipt for the referencing-commit scan (e.g. resolve against the pinned objects without calling `view.resolve`, or a wrapper that only records resolutions for ids in `accepted_ids`).

Epics ... stay on the materialized path,' but no test closes/verifies an epic ticket with verify.completion_pinned_ticket_view=true and asserts ticket_read_mode == 'materialized_epic' (or that no lazy view / atomic bundle is used).

evidence: ticket_view.py:378-383 docstring: 'Return pinned raw payloads for one event type, in event order.'
advisory.finding: `TicketObjectStore.event_payloads` (and `_load_state`) rely on `git ls-tree`/`cat-file --batch` path order (lexical) as a proxy for event/HLC order; the docstring on `PinnedTicketView.event_payloads` and `TicketObjectStore.event_payloads` promises 'in event order'. Lexical filename order equals HLC order only because event filenames are timestamp-prefixed — an implicit, undocumented coupling that would silently misorder payloads if the event-file naming scheme ever changes.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the verifier-failure fail-closed shaping still applies when `_verify_with_duration_metrics` (the documented monkeypatch seam) itself raises, or re-establish shaping at that seam.
evidence: close_precheck.py: `_verify_with_duration_metrics` docstring: "Compatibility seam for duration tests and transition-close monkeypatches."

close_precheck.py:700-731: `try: ... result = _verify_with_duration_metrics(...) finally: if ticket_view is not None: ticket_view.close()` — no `except` shapes an exception raised by a monkeypatched seam
completion_verifier_run.py:101-103: the fail-closed shaping now lives inside `run_close_verifier`, which `_verify_with_duration_metrics` delegates to but a monkeypatch would replace
dropped.finding: The verifier fail-closed error shaping (retryable->exit 11, else exit 1, with remedy hint and session-log degrade) was moved out of `_completion_precheck` into `run_close_verifier`, but the compatibility seam `_verify_with_duration_metrics` (documented as a transition-close monkeypatch target) now only re-raises whatever `run_close_verifier` raises. A test or caller that monkeypatches `_verify_with_duration_metrics` to raise a raw provider/LLM exception (as the old inline `try/except` around the verifier call would have caught and shaped) will now propagate that raw exception unshaped out of `_completion_precheck`, since the surrounding block is a bare `try/finally` with no `except`.
scenarios: A test/monkeypatch replacing `transition_close._verify_with_duration_metrics` (or `close_precheck._verify_with_duration_metrics`) to simulate a verifier outage
